flags.message: Proposal cover title 'Deck Building' and sole line item 'Build Deck as Above' describe no deck; the itemized scope is paver demo, slab, shed roof, screen enclosure, fireplace — deck component should carry zero and the 'posts integrated with existing deck framing' language is a carry-over error.

Post bearing is unresolved: proposal says posts tie into 'existing deck framing' over a demo'd paver patio, JBD prices 5 posts 'to approved bearing' with no turned-down footings, and the plan implies ≥7 posts on the long open side alone — post count and footing method must be locked before forms are set.

Fireplace system is undecided across sources (proposal 'masonry or framed', JBD priced 'manufactured', drawing p5 shows framed chase with brick veneer and Class A pipe); a masonry selection adds $4-8K+ materials and substantially more labor than the 98h carried, and the footing must be known before the slab pour.

JBD carries $0 permits and no inspection line items while the proposal states permitting is included; roof tie-in plus a solid-fuel appliance almost certainly require a building permit with framing and fireplace/chimney inspections — bundled_inspections and permit_items receive no JBD hours but should not be zero downstream.

JBD knee wall '~60 LF' vs takeoff ~36 LF (patio wraps an inside corner of the house, so only two sides are screened per plan p4); 60 LF would imply three open sides — JBD screen labor (48h) and material are likely overstated by roughly 40% if the plan is right.

Footprint: proposal ~12.5'×23.5' (294 sqft) vs drawing plan 22'-11"×11'-8" clear (267 sqft); knee wall 2' white vinyl (proposal) vs 3'-4 1/4" lap siding / ~3' beadboard (drawings); drawings also add a screened transom band, fascia/soffit, and painted brick chimney not in the proposal or JBD — per canon the proposal governs and these are logged, not adopted.

Roof structure 70h for a ~300 sqft single-plane shed roof with 19 rafters, one ledger, ~5-7 posts and 10 sheets of sheathing runs hot; a 3-person crew would normally frame and sheathe this in 2-2.5 days (~50h), with the tie-in and chimney box the only justifications for more.

WB fireplace structure 98h (90h GL) for a manufactured firebox in a ~6'-wide framed chase is heavy — a manufactured kit with Class A pipe is typically a 3-4 day, 2-person install (~50-65h); the number only makes sense if a CMU/masonry chase is really intended.

Screened enclosure 48h for ~36 LF of 2' knee wall, screen frames, one door and trim is on the high side (2-person crew ~3 days ≈ 48h is the ceiling, not the expectation), and is built on the 60 LF assumption flagged above.

Electrical 6h and $95 material carried for a scope with zero electrical; PM notes themselves say to get zero-electrical intent in writing — either this collapses to 0h or a customer add (fan/lights/GFIC) changes rough_meps materially.

No roof pitch, rafter/beam/ledger sizing, engineering, or chimney termination height exists in any source; roof area is carried as plan area (~300 sqft) with no slope factor, and the 10-3-2 check against the existing hip roof could force a taller chase than the 6' × ~3'-7" drawn.

Concrete patio is mapped to groundwork (foundation before framing) rather than concrete_landscape; downstream should not expect a separate flatwork phase after the shell, and landscaping/yard restoration is explicitly excluded by the JBD.

Fireplace structure split between structural_framing and rough_meps is a best-fit only — a solid-fuel chimney system is not an MEP trade, and if masonry is selected the work is a mason's scope that does not fit any Addition component cleanly.
